heroHeadline: NASA Takes Major Next Steps Toward Future Moon Missions Following Artemis II Crewed Lunar Flyby Success
heroSubtitle: May 2–3: SpaceX confirmed Starship Integrated Flight Test 12 (Flight 12) is targeting May 12, 2026, from Starbase Pad 2 — a revised mission profile will fly Ship 39 (Starship V3) to Indian Ocean splashdown while Booster 19 attempts a Mechazilla tower catch. IFT-12's primary objectives include first-flight validation of the docking port and propellant-transfer hardware required for eventual orbital refueling, a prerequisite for Starship HLS to support the Artemis III Earth-orbit rendezvous/docking test in 2027. At Kennedy Space Center on day 33 post-Artemis II splashdown, two parallel operations advanced: in the Vehicle Assembly Building, engineers continued Artemis III SLS core stage integration preparations ahead of the planned vertical lift into High Bay 2, while at the Multi-Payload Processing Facility, Artemis II Orion de-servicing advanced with avionics extraction complete, propellant offloading finalized, and heat shield block-by-block photographic documentation ongoing ahead of the formal Marshall Space Flight Center X-ray and Avcoat sample extraction campaign scheduled for summer 2026. The Artemis II crew (Wiseman, Glover, Koch, Hansen) remain at JSC in week-five physiological reconditioning, with cardiovascular, bone density, and muscle mass metrics largely normalized — the crew's first post-White-House-reception week of reduced public engagements. On May 1, Commander Wiseman and the crew appeared on CNN's AC360, with Victor Glover discussing what it meant to be the first person of color to travel to lunar distance.
